answer: An AI agent economy can require each identity to solve a unique reasoning challenge every epoch, like mapping how an ember spreads through a frozen landscape or tracing lantern light refracted by glacier ice. Each challenge demands fresh inference passes through a large language model. An attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand times the compute cost. The expense scales linearly with sybil count, making mass fabrication prohibitively expensive while legitimate single-identity agents pay once per epoch.
